arm-linux UNIT SET -- READ THIS BEFORE USING THE BIN TARBALL
============================================================
Added 2026-09-11.  This file is NOT mirrored inside any published tarball, so it
can be corrected without making an already-shipped artifact disagree with it.
VERSION.txt is byte-identical to the copy inside the v58 bin tarball (md5
01e0ba5003dc90ccff0e12e6a63a46e1) and is therefore left exactly as it shipped --
INCLUDING the line that tells you to pair the compiler with
vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz.  That line is not wrong, it is INCOMPLETE,
and this file is the correction.

WHAT CHANGED: THE PUBLISHED UNIT SET WAS RTL-ONLY
-------------------------------------------------
vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz ships 204 files -- 99 .ppu, 100 .o and 5
.rsj: the RTL and nothing else.  1547 package units (fcl-json, fcl-base, fcl-xml,
fpvectorial, paszlib, the rest) had been compiled for arm-linux and had never
been published.  So a user holding only the published bytes could build a program
that uses SysUtils and Classes, and could NOT build one that uses fpjson.

Measured, not assumed.  Same compiler, same command line, same source; the ONLY
axis that differs is the unit set:

    uses SysUtils, Classes;        old RTL-only set  rc=0     full set  rc=0
    uses SysUtils, fpjson;         old RTL-only set  rc=1     full set  rc=0

and the rc=1 is:

    pkgtest.pas(3,16) Fatal: Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgtest

AND THE OTHER HALF OF THAT TRAP: THE SUFFIX RULE DOES NOT TRAVEL
----------------------------------------------------------------
Added 2026-09-11.  "Use the -full one" is correct HERE, and correct nowhere else
BY NAME.  dist/aarch64-linux/ has no *-units-full file at all, and its
plain-named vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz IS its full set (3217
members, 1631 .ppu, fpjson present -- measured, with an impossible-unit-name
grep as the control).  Carrying this rule there by filename finds nothing and
reads as "aarch64 never got a full set", which is false.  The discriminator is
the member count, or simply whether fpjson.ppu is in the archive -- never the
suffix.  See dist/aarch64-linux/UNITS.txt.

WHAT TO DOWNLOAD
----------------
  vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-arm-linux-bin.tar.gz    the compiler
      1712348 bytes   md5 b9eae9c45dd73b28618cebe0f5a79b27

  vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units-full.tar.gz        the unit set  <-- USE THIS ONE
      82757332 bytes
      md5    6e92ffab6cb292c65dc0dc393a487164
      sha256 aca16ac314da1730e3253c71807d2a8249fc4e31c5f54f98a5a2438afa855030
      3496 files flat in units/arm-linux/:
        1646 .ppu   (99 RTL + 1547 package)
        1600 .o
         249 .rsj   (resource strings)
           1 .inc   (packages/gdbint gdbver.inc)
      The same full RTL+packages shape as the win64 and aarch64-linux sets.

  vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz             SUPERSEDED, still published
      3353006 bytes   md5 bd4fa9afca17ed8d4595ddb1cafb9960
      Kept byte-untouched because it has been downloadable since 2026-09-10 and
      anyone verifying it against its recorded hash must still succeed.  You do
      not need both: it is a PROVEN strict subset -- all 204 of its members were
      md5-compared against the same-named members of the full set, 0 differences.
      A NEW NAME was used rather than replacing the old file for exactly this
      reason.  Same name plus different bytes is indistinguishable from
      corruption to anyone who already has a copy.

Extract the bin tarball and the full units tarball into the same directory.  You
get bin/ppcarm and units/arm-linux/, and the compiler needs to be told where the
units are:

    ./bin/ppcarm -Fuunits/arm-linux -Flunits/arm-linux hello.pas

WHY THE UNITS SAY v54 AND THE COMPILER SAYS v58
-----------------------------------------------
The version stamp is MEASURED, not picked.  These PPUs were built 2026-09-10,
which was v54.  The stamp is nominal only:

    git diff --stat b7d2d9676e HEAD -- rtl/ packages/     -> EMPTY

RTL and package SOURCE did not move at all between v54 and v58.  Only compiler/
moved (8 files, 210 insertions).  The same version-mismatched pairing already
ships for win64 (v52 units + v58 binary) and aarch64-linux (v52 units + v58
binary), and it is the honest shape: restamping these v58 would claim a rebuild
that did not happen.

ONE UNIT IS OUT OF FAMILY, AND IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND:
1546 package PPUs are from 2026-09-10 14:xx, and
packages/gstreamer/units/arm-linux/gst.ppu is from 2026-09-11 01:07.  It loads
clean along with everything else.  It is recorded here only so nobody finds a
stray mtime and wonders what it means.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED, AND THE CHAIN MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ONE NUMBER
-----------------------------------------------------------------
1. LOADS: dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh arm-linux (compiler ppcrossarm) ->
   143/143 packages load clean, 0 problems, ZERO silent recompiles.
2. THE TARBALL HOLDS THOSE EXACT BYTES: all 3496 members md5-compared against
   the tree files the load check measured -> 0 mismatches.  Without this link,
   step 1 describes different bytes than the ones shipping.
3. EXTRACT TO RUNNING PROGRAM FROM THE PUBLISHED BYTES ONLY: both tarballs into
   an empty directory; a program using SysUtils, Classes AND fpjson compiled with
   -n so this host's installed FPC could supply nothing; output is "ELF 32-bit
   LSB executable, ARM, EABI5 version 1 (SYSV), statically linked"; it RAN and
   printed { "cpu" : "arm-linux", "bits" : 32 } -- NativeInt = 4, as it must be
   on 32-bit ARM.
4. NEGATIVE CONTROL FIRED: identical command with units/ renamed away ->
   rc=1, "hello.pas(1,15) Fatal: Can't find unit system used by hello".
   A check that cannot fail proves nothing.

THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: all of the above ran under qemu-arm-static on an
x86_64 host, with arm-linux-gnueabihf cross binutils supplying as/ld because this
host has no native ARM assembler.  qemu-user runs the real shipped bytes and real
ARM instruction encodings, so codegen and RTL defects DO surface -- but it is not
a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS EVER RUN THESE ON PHYSICAL 32-BIT ARM HARDWARE.  A
real board does not need the -XP cross-binutils prefix; it uses its own as/ld.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1123

VERIFY IT YOURSELF -- THIS IS EXECUTABLE, NOT ADVICE
----------------------------------------------------
Added 2026-09-11 (cycle 1126).  dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh runs the arm-linux
half of everything above end to end against the PUBLISHED bytes:

    sh dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh [workdir]

Exit 0 = every stage passed.  1 = a stage failed, and the message says which.
2 = this host is missing qemu/cross-binutils, or the workdir has under 2 GB free
(a complete run leaves 807 MB) -- so NOTHING WAS MEASURED.

THE -full VERSUS RTL-ONLY DISTINCTION AT THE TOP OF THIS FILE IS NOW ENFORCED,
NOT JUST DESCRIBED.  Measured today: with the -full tarball moved aside so the
resolver fell back to the 206-member RTL-only set, that script printed
"ARM RUNTIME PROOF: PASS" and exited 0 -- because every test it ran resolved
inside the RTL.  It now also compiles and runs a program that uses fpjson (a
PACKAGE unit), and the same substitution fails:

    pkgtest.pas(3,25) Fatal: Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgtest

Scored on that TEXT, never on the exit code.  Likewise, with no bin tarball in
this directory the script used to print "using " and then "tar (child): :
Cannot open: No such file or directory" at rc=2 -- which reads like a corrupt
download when the real cause is an empty directory.  It now says:

    FAIL no arm-linux bin tarball in <dir> (looked for
    vibepascal-v*-arm-linux-bin.tar.gz) -- NOTHING WAS TESTED; that is this
    tree, not a bad artifact

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1126
